edition: Weekend edition — catch up on the week

items.title: 121 W. Wacker office tower sells at a 75% discount
items.summary: Two local investors bought the 441K SF riverfront tower for $30M — it traded for $118.5M in 2018.

items.title: Cushman & Wakefield's global HQ sells at a 45% discount
items.summary: A Prime Finance affiliate and Hines paid about $115M for 225 W. Wacker, down from $210M in 2020.

items.title: 27-story Mag Mile office tower heads to foreclosure auction
items.summary: 625 N. Michigan Ave. goes to auction Dec. 28 after its owners defaulted on a roughly $51M loan.

items.title: Developer plots 1.3M SF industrial project in Joliet
items.summary: Logistics Property Co. closed on a 74-acre Houbolt Road site, its fourth Chicago-area development site in a year.

items.title: Mall redevelopments bring walkable living to the suburbs
items.summary: Developers are turning malls into mixed-use projects where residents can live, shop and eat without driving.

items.title: Glenstar hires industry vet to grow its logistics arm
items.summary: The office-focused Chicago firm brought on Tim Thompson, who built 10M+ SF of industrial at HSA, to expand.

items.title: Prologis exec on its Chicago industrial strategy
items.summary: Prologis keeps building infill sites with high barriers to entry while the regional pipeline shrinks to a third of its 2022 level.

items.title: Illinois unveils 240 tracts for Opportunity Zones 2.0
items.summary: The state got federal approval for a new OZ map after calling the first round's results in Illinois uneven.

items.title: Hynes wins Cook County assessor, vows tax stability
items.summary: Pat Hynes won the assessor race easily — a big deal for commercial owners' property tax bills.
